meta.title: Resources | GPODH
meta.description: An ongoing list of great resources from the podcast and beyond: articles, organisations, and tools at the intersection of digital health and underserved communities.

hero.title: Useful reading. Essential organisations.
hero.intro: An ongoing list of resources we collect along the way. Articles, organisations, frameworks, and funding sources at the intersection of digital health and underserved communities.

shubstack.title: Shubstack
shubstack.body: Shubs writes regularly on current issues in digital health, reflects on podcast conversations, and shares perspectives on what's changing in the field. A companion to the podcast. Read between episodes.

footerNote: This list is updated periodically. Got a recommendation? [Let us know](/contact)

items.label: Standing Together Initiative
items.description: We spoke to Dr Xiao Liu in Episode 1 about what actionable things we can do about health data poverty. This is a great resource.

items.label: Rowena Luk's Africa Health Ventures
items.description: About the digital health investment landscape in Africa. Listen to our discussion with Rowena on Episode 14.

items.label: The Agency Fund
items.description: We like their view on what needs to change in funding.

items.label: The 5 Stages of Regulatory Grief
items.description: Regulatory expert Hugh Harvey of Hardian Health, who we spoke to in Episode 13, wrote and spoke about this excellent article on regulatory strategy pitfalls.

items.label: Seyi Abimbola: The Foreign Gaze
items.description: Seyi writes compellingly about how global health needs to change. He recently published a book called The Foreign Gaze. Read it. Be changed.

items.label: Community Health Impact Coalition: Community Health Worker video series
items.description: Check out their series on community health workers. Essential viewing.

items.label: Geneva Digital Health Hub
items.description: GDHD lead a great community called Implementome, for anyone implementing digital health and AI tools across the world. Also a great conference every year. Check out the episode we did with GDHD director Caroline Perrin (episode 15).

items.label: WHO Global Strategy on Digital Health 2020–2025
items.description: The foundational WHO framework for digital health.

items.label: ITU Digital Inclusion Framework
items.description: Addressing connectivity and access as prerequisites for digital health.

items.label: PHCPI Primary Health Care Framework
items.description: How digital tools fit into primary care strengthening.

items.label: MAPS Toolkit
items.description: WHO framework for mHealth assessment and planning.

items.label: GRADE Approach
items.description: Grading the quality of evidence for clinical decision making.

items.label: Digital Health Monitor (WHO)
items.description: Tracking digital health policy progress globally.

items.label: Classification of Digital Health Interventions (WHO)
items.description: The taxonomy for understanding what digital health tools do.

items.label: Consolidated Telemedicine Implementation Guide (WHO)
items.description: Practical guidance for telemedicine deployment.

items.label: Digital Health Country Assessments (ITU/WHO)
items.description: Country-level readiness and capacity assessments.

items.label: Lancet Digital Health
items.description: Peer-reviewed research on digital health interventions, including extensive coverage of LMICs.

items.label: The Digital Health Atlas
items.description: Mapping digital health implementations across the world.

items.label: GSMA Mobile for Development Insights
items.description: How mobile technology is being used in emerging markets.

items.label: Digital Square
items.description: A PATH-led initiative to strengthen global goods for digital health.

items.label: Access Health International
items.description: Advisory on health reform and systems strengthening.

items.label: Resolve to Save Lives
items.description: Cardiovascular disease prevention at scale in LMICs.

items.label: Grand Challenges Canada
items.description: Funds bold ideas with the potential to save and improve lives in LMICs, including digital health and AI applications. The Stars in Global Health programme is particularly relevant.

items.label: Grand Challenges (Gates Foundation)
items.description: Open calls for innovation addressing health challenges in the developing world. Regularly funds digital health, diagnostics, and AI in global health.

items.label: Wellcome Trust: Discovery Research and Innovations
items.description: Funds research across global health including digital and data science applications. Their health inequities and infectious disease portfolios are relevant to LMIC digital health.

items.label: The Skoll Foundation
items.description: Supports social entrepreneurs tackling systemic global challenges. Several Skoll awardees work in digital health and health equity.

items.label: Omidyar Network
items.description: Invests in market-based and policy approaches to increase inclusion and opportunity. Relevant for digital health ventures addressing underserved populations.

items.label: Google.org
items.description: Google's philanthropic arm funds nonprofits and social enterprises using technology for social impact, including AI for health in underserved settings.

items.label: Rockefeller Foundation: Health Initiative
items.description: Long-standing funder of global health innovation, with a focus on health system strengthening and equity. Active in digital health and AI.

items.label: USAID Digital Development
items.description: USAID's digital development team funds and supports digital tools and infrastructure in developing countries. Their Digital Strategy sets the framework.

items.label: IDRC: International Development Research Centre
items.description: Canadian public funder supporting research-based solutions in developing countries. Strong portfolio in digital health, AI for development, and data systems.

items.label: The Fleming Fund
items.description: UK-funded programme supporting countries in generating and using data to tackle antimicrobial resistance. A useful model for health data funding in LMICs.

items.label: World Bank Digital Development Partnership
items.description: A multi-donor trust fund supporting countries in developing digital infrastructure and policies. Useful for government and systems-level digital health projects.

items.label: The Global Fund
items.description: Primary funder of HIV, TB, and malaria programmes globally. Increasingly funds digital health components including surveillance, supply chain, and community health systems.
